$comment: International catalog for `fetch.py` — language-neutral or English.
Per-language material lives in a sibling overlay: `catalog.it.json`,
`catalog.fr.json`, ... loaded on top of this one with `--lang it`.
An overlay entry with a NEW id is added; an entry reusing an id from this
file REPLACES it (that is how `ifixit` becomes the Italian edition rather
than a second 3.6 GB copy of the same guides).
This file holds no URLs. Kiwix archives are date-stamped and there is no
'latest' symlink, so any URL written here would rot; fetch.py resolves the
current filename, size and SHA-256 from the live Kiwix catalog instead.
Add your own entries freely — this is data, not code:
Anything with a `url` is downloaded verbatim, so any HTTP source works.
Flavours, for Wikipedia-style archives: `maxi` = full text + images,
`nopic` = full text, `mini` = lead section only. `mini` is a good index
and a poor manual: procedures live in the sections it drops.

presets.base: Starting set (~1.4 GB): emergency medicine, water, food, repair thinking. Fits anywhere.
presets.health: Medicine in depth, human and animal.
presets.practical: Making, growing, fixing and powering things.
presets.wikipedia: Full-text encyclopedia and dictionaries (replaces the `mini` editions).
presets.reference: Long-form reference: public-domain books, taxonomy, courses.

entries.note: Field and emergency medicine books. Tiny, dense, written for no-hospital conditions.
Water collection, storage and purification. The first thing that runs out.
Preserving and preparing food without a cold chain.
The post-disaster resource library: shelter, sanitation, safety, salvage.
Knots, lashings, ladders and sutures, illustrated. Absurdly small for what it covers.
Appropriate technology: build it from what exists locally. The core 'rebuild' wiki.
NHS drugs A-Z: doses, interactions, contraindications.
WikEM: the largest open emergency-medicine reference. Written for the acute case.
WikiMed, Wikipedia's medical corpus. `maxi`: in medicine the diagrams are the content.
MDWiki medical encyclopedia: deeper clinical detail than WikiMed.
Military medical manuals: surgery and trauma care without a hospital behind you.
Veterinary reference. Where there are animals they are food, transport and work.
US civil-protection preparedness guidance, hazard by hazard.
Off-grid energy: solar, micro-hydro, biogas, storage.
Step-by-step repair guides. Replaces nothing, keeps everything running.
Wikibooks: actual manuals rather than encyclopedia entries.
US Army field manuals: survival, first aid, engineering, water. Big; take it deliberately.
Home Improvement Q&A: plumbing, electrics, structure — someone had your exact problem.
Gardening & landscaping Q&A: growing food, pests, soil.
The Great Outdoors Q&A: navigation, shelter, cold, water in the field.
Woodworking Q&A: hand-tool technique when the power tools stop.
Sustainable living Q&A: low-input households.
Cooking Q&A: substitutions, preservation, food safety.
Fermentation Q&A. Fermenting is preservation before it is a hobby.
Amateur radio Q&A: antennas and propagation, i.e. communication after the network.
Electronics Q&A. Large; take it if you repair boards rather than swap them.
Top 1M English articles, full text. A third of `en_all_nopic`, most of the value.
Travel guides: what a place has, where its water is, how to reach it.
Public-domain agriculture. Pre-industrial methods, written when they were the method.
Public-domain technology: forges, mills, machining, construction. Large.
Public-domain medicine. Historical — read it next to WikiMed, not instead of it.
Taxonomy of everything living. Identification still needs a regional field guide.
Course material: teaching, not just looking up.
Biology Q&A.
Chemistry Q&A: what reacts with what, and what that costs you.
Physics Q&A. Large.
